names: Puhi Kai Iti / Cook Landing Site

new_destinations.note: Wairoa and Māhia are only two kept places 46 km apart; too few for a destination, so both stand alone.

lowest_kept_note: Several kept places have views 0 because Wikipedia has no article or a redirect; they are kept on counted Wikivoyage and DOC sources, not on views.

stronger_left_out.name: Gisborne
stronger_left_out.reason: Existing destination 'gisborne'; listed so the run judged it, nothing to place.

stronger_left_out.name: Te Araroa Trail
stronger_left_out.reason: For: Wikivoyage page for the 3,000 km national trail. Against: a country-long linear feature, not one place in this region; it needs a single main-access point and a cross-region duplicate check; Lake Waikaremoana and Whirinaki already cover its stretch here.

stronger_left_out.name: Poverty Bay
stronger_left_out.reason: Region-scale bay; its beaches and city are the visits, not the bay as a site.

stronger_left_out.name: Rhythm & Vines
stronger_left_out.reason: Annual music festival, an event not a permanent place.

stronger_left_out.name: Whangara
stronger_left_out.reason: Film location in a small settlement on Māori land; nothing public to see or do.

stronger_left_out.name: Tolaga Bay
stronger_left_out.reason: For: Wikivoyage and DOC name the bay and settlement. Against: its draw is the wharf and Cooks Cove, both already spots; Wikivoyage says "small bay and settlement popular with local holiday makers", so a near-duplicate of the wharf spot.

stronger_left_out.name: Ruatoria
stronger_left_out.reason: Service town; no sight or activity named.

stronger_left_out.name: Te Kaha
stronger_left_out.reason: For: Wikivoyage lists it; the main service stop on the northern coast. Against: a small settlement with no named sight or activity; Wikivoyage describes it as a fishermen/holiday community.

stronger_left_out.name: East Cape
stronger_left_out.reason: A region/road journey rather than a single place; the places along it (lighthouse, bays) are the spots, and the cape itself is covered by East Cape Lighthouse.

stronger_left_out.name: Tikitiki
stronger_left_out.reason: Village with no draw of its own beyond its church (judged separately).

stronger_left_out.name: Te Urewera National Park
stronger_left_out.reason: Kept by the skeptic but not a new spot: the destination 'te-urewera' already exists (see existing_fixes).

stronger_left_out.name: Mount Hikurangi
stronger_left_out.reason: For: DOC names the 1,752 m sacred peak, first mainland point to see the sunrise. Against: Ngāti Porou sacred maunga with permission/guided access, long tramp, rarely visited, one source. Coords OSM -37.9189,178.0607.

stronger_left_out.name: Te Puia Springs
stronger_left_out.reason: No counted source; no visitor description of a public hot-spring venue.

stronger_left_out.name: Tuai
stronger_left_out.reason: Village with no counted source or sight. Belongs to the Hawke's Bay pass.

stronger_left_out.name: SS Talune
stronger_left_out.reason: No counted source; a wreck for divers. Belongs to the Hawke's Bay pass.

stronger_left_out.name: Waipiro Bay
stronger_left_out.reason: No counted source; small settlement.

stronger_left_out.name: Matawai
stronger_left_out.reason: Small roadside township with nothing to see or do named by the guide.

stronger_left_out.name: Gisborne City Vintage Railway
stronger_left_out.reason: No counted source (Wikipedia/OSM only).

stronger_left_out.name: Titirangi
stronger_left_out.reason: Near-duplicate of existing spot gisborne-1 (Titirangi / Kaiti Hill).

stronger_left_out.name: Akuaku
stronger_left_out.reason: No counted source; ruins with no visitor guide.

stronger_left_out.name: Mōtū
stronger_left_out.reason: Gateway settlement with no sight of its own.

stronger_left_out.name: Hackfalls Arboretum
stronger_left_out.reason: No counted source (Wikipedia protected-areas list only); mostly private gardens.

stronger_left_out.name: Whakarua Park
stronger_left_out.reason: Local park, no counted source.

stronger_left_out.name: St Mary's Church, Tikitiki
stronger_left_out.reason: For: celebrated carved/woven Māori Anglican war-memorial church on SH35, a classic East Cape stop. Against: no counted visitor source found, a local church, interior access not confirmed (church benchmark rejects).

stronger_left_out.name: Harry Barker Reserve
stronger_left_out.reason: Local reserve, no counted source.

stronger_left_out.name: Gisborne Botanical Gardens
stronger_left_out.reason: No counted source (Wikipedia/OSM only); ordinary city park.

stronger_left_out.name: Maungahaumia

stronger_left_out.name: Mount Arowhana
stronger_left_out.reason: No counted source; remote peak.

stronger_left_out.name: Mōkau Falls
stronger_left_out.reason: No counted source (Wikipedia category only). Belongs to the Hawke's Bay pass.

stronger_left_out.name: Papatea Bay
stronger_left_out.reason: Same site as Raukokore Church; near-duplicate.

stronger_left_out.name: Whakaki Lagoon
stronger_left_out.reason: No counted source; wetland with no visitor facilities named. Belongs to the Hawke's Bay pass.

stronger_left_out.name: Raukūmara Conservation Park
stronger_left_out.reason: Remote 115,000 ha backcountry park with no facilities and the Wilderness Area closed to recreation; rarely visited; one source.

stronger_left_out.name: Gisborne Farmers Market
stronger_left_out.reason: Saturday-morning market only; weekly market fails the always-there test. needs_coordinates.

review_list.reason: For: Wikivoyage names the isolated shoreline church at Papatea Bay, a photographed roadside icon (and Papatea Bay is the same place). Against: a church seen mainly from outside, ten-minute stop. Needs coordinates (OSM, not memory).

benchmark: Region-level benchmarks: Gisborne has none of the national benchmark places (Red Rocks, Kapiti Island, Ohakune Carrot and so on lie in other regions). Negative benchmarks hold: no hospital, civic building, minor memorial or weekly market kept (Gisborne Farmers Market and Rhythm & Vines rejected). Pipiriki-type gateway villages (Te Kaha, Tikitiki, Ruatoria, Mōtū) rejected or sent to review.
